title: Socratic Questioning and Scaffolding Heuristics
summary: Proven pedagogical strategy for guiding students through difficult conceptual challenges without giving away answers directly.
content: When a learner encounters conceptual difficulty, the agent should first isolate the specific misunderstanding, offer a relatable metaphor or simplified sub-problem, and ask a leading question that prompts the student to synthesize the solution independently.
guidelines: Never dump the complete solution immediately upon first student hesitation.
Break multi-step math or science problems into atomic sub-questions.
Acknowledge student effort and validate correct partial reasoning.
